dedupe_keys.name: wayside energy storage for regenerative braking on a real italian railway infrastructure

description: This study by L. Alfieri, Luigi Battistelli and Mario Pagano of the University of Naples Federico II and Parthenope University of Naples, published in IET Electrical Systems in Transportation in 2019, examines the introduction of wayside energy storage systems (WESS) into a real Italian railway infrastructure to exploit train braking energy. Coverage: a WESS can be integrated into urban mass transit and long-distance railway lines as smart storage that recovers surplus regenerative braking energy, stabilises grid voltage and reduces peak power demand; the authors propose a method based on a simulator of the WESS integrated into the infrastructure and run dynamic simulations with real operating data of the system and its vehicles, reporting energy and power exchange and economic aspects. Format and access: a journal article. Licence and cost: closed access, paid. Caveats: the abstract was the part read, and the line is not named in it. The method can size and place traction energy storage in rail power capacity planning and optimisation models. It relates to the New York City subway wayside storage study and the ELECTRA traction substation dataset in the catalogue.
